findings.body:
**Use the effective start timeout from the target template.**

If `TimeoutStartSec=30s` is followed by `TimeoutSec=5min`, systemd applies the five-minute start timeout. The adapter records 30s and, at Line 1803, gives `start` 90s. A healthy 120s start then times out after the mask has been released. Resolve both directives in file order before deriving the budget and command timeout. A template with only `TimeoutStartSec=` should keep its current behavior. ([freedesktop.org](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/256/systemd.service.html))
findings.title: Use the effective start timeout from the target template.

findings.body:
**Enforce the configured maximum on the actual completion window.**

With a required window of 180s, `max_completion_window=300`, and `completion_timeout=3600`, both checks pass. Line 1843 then sets a one-hour deadline instead of respecting the five-minute cap. Reject an explicit timeout above the cap before mutation. Keep overrides between the required duration and the cap valid.
findings.title: Enforce the configured maximum on the actual completion window.

findings.body:
**Keep the previous saved timeout when an empty assignment is ignored.**

For a saved service with `TimeoutStartSec=5min` followed by an empty `TimeoutStartSec=`, systemd keeps the five-minute value. This branch discards it. If the pinned template specifies 30s, rollback releases the mask and gives `start` only 90s. A healthy two-minute start then times out during recovery. Treat the empty assignment as ignored and retain the prior valid value. An inactive snapshot still needs no start timeout. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/systemd/systemd/v255/src/core/load-fragment.c))
findings.title: Keep the previous saved timeout when an empty assignment is ignored.

findings.body:
**Read pinned template names without Git pathname quoting.**

With Git pathname quoting enabled, an extra `crq-tick-copy-é.timer` produces a quoted record. The prefix check drops the record, so the final inventory check never sees the undeclared timer. Read `git ls-tree -z --name-only` as bytes and split on NUL. This preserves the declared names and sends the extra entry to the refusal check. ([git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-ls-tree.html?utm_source=openai))
findings.title: Read pinned template names without Git pathname quoting.

findings.body:
**Parse a space between the timeout magnitude and unit.**

Systemd accepts `TimeoutStartSec=5 min`. This parser consumes `5`, then fails at `min`. For an active saved service, Line 1426 can then substitute the shorter pinned timeout. With a pinned 30s timeout, a healthy two-minute start fails during recovery after the mask is released. Parse optional whitespace before the unit, and cover both `5 min` and `5min`. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/systemd/systemd/v255/src/basic/time-util.c))
findings.title: Parse a space between the timeout magnitude and unit.

findings.body:
**Check the deadline before accepting completion evidence.**

If the last poll returns `None` and the sleep resumes after the deadline, the next poll can return a record that arrived late. The adapter returns that record without checking the clock. Check the deadline before the next poll and again before accepting the result, so a port call that returns late cannot bypass the bound. An on-time record should still pass.
findings.title: Check the deadline before accepting completion evidence.

findings.body:
**Include randomized delay in the timer bound.**

A timer with `OnUnitInactiveSec=1min`, `AccuracySec=1s`, and `RandomizedDelaySec=10min` gets a 61s timer bound. With a 30s oneshot, the adapter waits 151s for completion. If systemd selects a 5min delay, the second invocation cannot start before the adapter times out. Include the maximum randomized delay in the bound, or refuse this timer before fencing. An omitted delay should still contribute zero. ([freedesktop.org](https://freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.timer.html?utm_source=openai))
findings.title: Include randomized delay in the timer bound.

findings.body:
**Refuse target services that remain active after the first invocation.**

A bounded `Type=oneshot` target with `RemainAfterExit=yes` passes this check. After the explicit start, systemd keeps the service active. The restored timer does not restart an active service, so the second distinct completion cannot arrive. Reject this target configuration in preflight. Keep restoration of a saved service separate. ([freedesktop.org](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/249/systemd.timer.html?utm_source=openai))
findings.title: Refuse target services that remain active after the first invocation.

findings.body:
**Check that repeated recovery preserves the restored fixture.**

A repeat can return `2` and leave the journal unchanged after modifying the service or staged file. The repeat checks still pass. Compare the restored service, staging path, and stable activator configuration before and after the repeat. Do not require an active timer's completion log to stay unchanged.






Also applies to: 1562-1563, 2768-2769
findings.title: Check that repeated recovery preserves the restored fixture.

findings.body:
**Require the injected kill in each interruption proof.**

An ordinary exit `1` after the adapter writes the `drained` journal and masks the service passes the status check. The state checks cannot distinguish that error from an injected kill. Require the expected signal exit status, as `recover_kill_phase` does at Line 1342. Keep the journal and fence checks to verify where the switch stopped. On POSIX, Python reports direct child termination by a signal as a negative return code. ([docs.python.org](https://docs.python.org/3/library/subprocess.html))






Also applies to: 1482-1482, 1505-1505, 1591-1591, 1714-1714, 1734-1734, 2688-2688
findings.title: Require the injected kill in each interruption proof.

findings.body:
**Keep the canonical matrix artifact when a custom label is supplied.**

A successful boundary with `--label` writes only the custom filename. Its observe phase reads the canonical case filename at Line 1770. On a clean guest, that file is missing. On a reused guest, it can contain old evidence. Always write the canonical matrix artifact, or reject custom labels for phases with a fixed downstream filename.
findings.title: Keep the canonical matrix artifact when a custom label is supplied.

findings.body:
**Reject pending jobs in the matrix drain check.**

`_owned_work` accepts an empty cgroup with a waiting service start job. It returns the job for reporting, but both matrix callers continue without checking the list. Require a successful, empty job observation for `UNIT` and `TIMER` before the guest accepts the boundary or proceeds to recovery.
findings.title: Reject pending jobs in the matrix drain check.

findings.body:
**Validate the completion evidence in the retained journal.**

Both activator switches can pass if stdout contains valid completions but the new journal omits them. The fence checks the on-disk transaction ID and outcome only. The switch-back reports the on-disk summary without validating it. Run the completion checks against the new journal and confirm that stdout identifies that journal.






Also applies to: 2666-2667
findings.title: Validate the completion evidence in the retained journal.

findings.body:
**Validate the full completion evidence in the activator fence proof.**

`activators_fence` accepts two log invocation IDs in reverse sequence order. It also accepts a journal sequence that differs from the log sequence for the same invocation. Use `validate_completed(..., unit=REPAIR_UNIT)` here, and keep the check that neither invocation appeared during the pause.
findings.title: Validate the full completion evidence in the activator fence proof.

findings.body:
**Clean up when the paused observation fails.**

If `during()` raises after it creates `REPAIR_TRIGGER`, `cli_paused` does not reap the child, and `activators_fence` skips trigger removal and blocker cleanup. On callback failure, terminate and reap the switch before removing the pause marker. Put the caller's fixture cleanup in `finally`. Keep marker removal as the release step on success.






Also applies to: 2485-2488
findings.title: Clean up when the paused observation fails.

findings.body:
**Bind each drain phase to its named seed.**

`drain-alive --seed ambiguous` runs the ambiguity proof and saves it as `drain-alive.json`. The proof can pass without testing live owned work. Derive the seed from the phase name, or reject a conflicting `--seed` before setup.
findings.title: Bind each drain phase to its named seed.

findings.body:
**Undo inventory mutations when observation fails.**

If `repair_units()` raises during `unsafe-metadata`, `run_case` leaves the drop-in at mode `0666`. A retry starts with the wrong inventory and can fail the first refusal case for the wrong reason. Run the matching cleanup in `finally` after injecting the defect.
findings.title: Undo inventory mutations when observation fails.

findings.body:
**Protect drain fixture setup with the cleanup scope.**

If the owned seed succeeds but the unrelated process fails to launch, the phase exits before `finally`. The live child and run metadata remain. The harvest case leaves run metadata even though its child has exited. Enter the cleanup scope before creating either fixture and register each resource as soon as it is acquired.






Also applies to: 1082-1083, 1207-1208
findings.title: Protect drain fixture setup with the cleanup scope.

findings.body:
**Keep the timer fence durable across restart, or relax the observe check.**

The observe check at `apps/crq-python/ops/vm-unit-switch-guest.py:1806-1807` requires `crq-tick.timer` to be `inactive` or `failed` after a restart or reboot. The durable fence does not keep the timer from starting. `prepare_fixture` links the timer into `timers.target.wants` and requires it to be `enabled`. The drain path stops the activator units and masks only the service. After a user-manager start, `timers.target` can start the enabled timer while the service stays masked. In that case the observe phase fails before the recovery checks at lines 1816-1817.

The fence must either stop the timer from starting after the boundary, or the check must accept an active timer whose service is masked and cannot run work. The choice between these is a policy decision. The proof must match the chosen behavior. A runtime restart test has not been run.
findings.title: Keep the timer fence durable across restart, or relax the observe check.
